title: Protocol
description:
The root the schema is generated from.

Every type a client has to name, reachable from one place. schemars walks it and emits each reachable type once, under `definitions`, so the field names here are an index and nothing ever serialises as a `Protocol`.

Aspect.description:
What a capability is *about*.

The wire names are pinned per variant rather than derived, because two of them (`mem.read`, `mem.write`) are dotted and no `rename_all` rule produces a dot.

oneOf.description: Spawning a sub-agent or a process.
Reaching a host over the network.
Contributing a renderer for a surface kind.

Budget.description: What a turn is allowed to spend.

max_micro_usd.description: How much money, in micro-USD. `None` means unmetered.

max_tokens.description: How many tokens, input and output together.

wall_clock_ms.description: How long, in milliseconds of wall clock.

oneOf.description: A parent was cancelled, so this was too.

Capability.description:
One aspect and the scope it is granted over.

An **empty** `scope` means unqualified: the whole aspect, not nothing. That is what makes an unscoped parent wider than a scoped child, which is the direction narrowing needs.

scope.description: The names or patterns it covers. Empty means unqualified.

text.description: The cell's text, already formatted by whoever knows the units.

Choice.description: One option of a [`SurfaceKind::Question`] or of a choice [`Field`].

value.description: What is sent back on selection.

Consent.description:
How often the user has to be asked.

Ordered `Never < Once < Always`, and narrowing takes the minimum: a child that asks every time cannot be promoted to a child that never asks.

oneOf.description: Allowed once the user says so, each time.

ConsentAnswerKind.description:
The answer to a [`ConsentPrompt`].

Four answers, not two: "yes" and "yes, and stop asking" are different decisions, and so are "no" and "no, ever".

ConsentPrompt.description: What is being asked for, and why.

id.description: The handle an answer is matched to.

reason.description: Why, in words a person can act on.

rule.description: The rule that requires the ask, when one does.

surface.description: Something to show alongside the question — the diff that is about to be written, the command that is about to run.

oneOf.description: An image, inline and base64. A provider without an `images` capability rejects a message carrying one rather than dropping it silently.
The model asking for a tool.

input.description: The arguments, already validated against the tool's schema.

oneOf.description:
What happened.

Carries the same [`Outcome`] the `tool.settled` frame carries — one shape for "what happened", whether it is being shown to a person or fed back to a model. That is what makes a denial identical in the transcript and on the wire, instead of a rendered apology in one and a structured value in the other.

Reasoning the provider exposed.

Kept rather than dropped: every current provider emits it, the transcript is the audit record, and a turn tree that silently discards what the model was thinking cannot be replayed faithfully.

Contribution.description:
What an extension added to the session.

`kind` is a plain enum here. The derive macro that keeps it in step with the extension's manifest — so that a manifest promising a tool and a crate contributing a renderer is a build error rather than a surprise — is the extension host's (plan 06).

kind.description: What kind of thing it is.

name.description: Its name, unqualified: the extension is already known.

ContributionKind.description: The kinds of thing an extension can contribute.

oneOf.description: A tool the model can call.
A renderer for a custom surface kind.
A grader for the eval runner.
A named view over the session.

text.description: The line itself, without its leading marker.

DiffLineKind.description: What a line of a diff is.

data.description: Anything structured a client could use.

retryable.description: Whether the same thing, tried again, might work.

oneOf.description: The connection. Nothing else will arrive.
The session. Other sessions are fine.

Event.description:
Kernel to client.

Every variant carries a `seq`: a client detects a gap by arithmetic and re-attaches with `since`, which is only possible if the ordering is on the frame rather than implied by the transport.

seq.description: Where this sits in the session's order.
Where this sits in the session's order.
Where this sits in the session's order.

oneOf.description: A tool call ended, one way or another.

seq.description: Where this sits in the session's order.

deadline_ms.description: How long there is to answer before the default applies.

seq.description: Where this sits in the session's order.
Where this sits in the session's order.
Where this sits in the session's order.

label.description: What is shown next to it.

name.description: The key this field's value is submitted under.

required.description: Whether the form can be submitted without it.

oneOf.description: A line of text that must not be echoed, logged or stored.
A number, collected as text and parsed by whoever declared the field.

Grant.description: What a subject is allowed to do.

capabilities.description: The capabilities, one entry per aspect-and-scope.

Hunk.description: One changed region of a file.

new_start.description: First line of the region in the new file, 1-based.

old_start.description: First line of the region in the old file, 1-based.

LoadOutcome.description: The result of trying to load one extension.

oneOf.description: It loaded and did everything it promised.

It loaded, and something it promised is missing.

The interesting case, and the reason this is an enum rather than a `Result`: half an extension is usable, and saying which half is what stops a user hunting for a tool that quietly never registered.

problems.description: What is missing, in words a person can act on.

oneOf.description: It was tried and it did not work.

LoadStage.description: How far loading got before it stopped.

oneOf.description: Resolving its dependencies and its version requirements.
Linking the code: dynamic library, wasm module, child process.
The person, or a tool result being handed back.

Outcome.description:
How something turned out.

The type that makes "a denial is a value" real at every layer: the tool registry returns it, the transcript stores it, the wire carries it, the renderer draws it. Nothing anywhere raises a denial as an error, because an error would have to be rendered by whoever caught it, and then two layers would be describing the same refusal in two different ways.

surface.description: What to show, when there is something to show.

value.description: What to feed back to the model, when that differs from what is shown.

oneOf.description: Policy said no. The rule is named so the refusal can be explained and argued with, rather than being an opaque "not allowed".

reason.description: Why, in words a person can act on.

oneOf.description: It worked, but produced more than it was allowed to emit.
The extension that owns it is no longer loaded.
The tools visible in a session.
What is loaded, and how it went — see [`crate::load::LoadOutcome`].
The profiles a session can be created from.

Request.description:
Client to kernel.

Every variant carries an `id`, because every response has to name what it is answering. It is repeated per variant rather than lifted to a struct field because serde cannot express a struct-level field alongside an internally tagged enum — a test asserts that no variant lost it.

The tags are **dotted** and spelled out one by one. No `rename_all` rule produces a dot, so an added variant without an explicit `rename` would show up as `turn-submit` instead of `turn.submit`; the tag test catches exactly that.

profile.description: Which profile to build it from.

oneOf.description: Attach to an existing session, optionally replaying from a sequence number the client already has.

since.description: Replay from just after this. Absent means from the start.

oneOf.description: Answer a surface: a form submitted, a choice picked.

SkipReason.description:
Why an extension was not loaded at all.

A **closed** set. "It did not load" is a thing a user has to be able to act on, and free text cannot be grouped, counted or matched against a rule.

oneOf.description: Not built for this platform or this harness version.
Something it depends on is not there.

StackDir.description: Which way a [`SurfaceKind::Stack`] lays its children out.

Status.description: How far along whatever produced this surface is.

oneOf.description: In flight; more patches are coming.

Surface.description: A surface, with the handle a patch addresses it by and how far along it is.

id.description: The handle. Absent for a surface nothing will ever patch.

rows.description: The body. Every row is expected to be `columns.len()` long.

oneOf.description: Something taking a while. `done`/`total` absent means indeterminate.
An append-only channel. The content arrives as [`SurfacePatch::Append`], which is the hot path.
A question the run is blocked on.

deadline_ms.description: How long there is to answer.

default.description: What is used if the deadline passes.

free.description: Whether an answer outside `choices` is accepted.

multi.description: Whether more than one may be picked.

oneOf.description: Markdown. `complete` is false while it is still streaming, so a client knows not to trust a half-open code fence.

complete.description: Whether the last patch has arrived.

oneOf.description: Anything an extension brought its own renderer for.

fallback.description:
What to show instead, for a client that has no such renderer.

Mandatory, and a `Box<Surface>` rather than an `Option`: a custom surface nobody can draw is a blank hole in a transcript, so the type refuses to express one.

kind.description: `<ext>.<name>`, so two extensions cannot claim one renderer.

SurfacePatch.description:
A change to a surface already on screen.

The whole point of the surface protocol: a streaming tool sends one [`SurfacePatch::Append`] per chunk rather than a whole new surface, so the hot path is a string and not a tree.

oneOf.description: Add to the end of a stream or a markdown body.
Set one field, addressed by a path of keys.

path.description: The path from the surface's root to the field.

id.description: A stable handle, so a patch can update one item.

TextStyle.description: A hint about how a run of text is meant, never a colour.

oneOf.description: Secondary: a count, a path, a timing.

children.description: Its children. A leaf has none.

id.description: A stable handle, when the client needs to address this node.

cache_hits.description: Tokens served from a provider-side prompt cache.

micro_usd.description: Cost in micro-USD, when the provider reports one.

attachments.description: Anything else they attached: images, a pasted tool result.

branch.description: Which branch of the turn tree to submit on. Absent means the current one; present means "re-run from here", which is how an edited turn forks rather than overwrites.
